meta.title: The Rat Race

guide.title: Guide
guide.news: Every round opens with the paper: some headlines hint at the next two years, and not all of them come true. You can read it again from the paper button at the top.
guide.cards: Life deals you a few cards every round. Each choice shows what it costs and what it brings before you pick, with the odds where there are dice, and it cannot be taken back.
guide.finance: Now your money. Nothing here happens until you play the round, and the line above the button tells you the exact [cash](cash) you will have afterwards. Start in Portfolio.
guide.ledger: Two years went by: this is everything that came in and went out. Prices moved after you played, so what you own is worth something new.
guide.ratRace: The bar at the top is the whole game: your [passive income](passive) against what your life costs. Cover the cost two rounds running and you are out of the rat race.
guide.goal: A life is {rounds} rounds of two years, from {from} to {to}. Your score adds your [net worth](netWorth), which gives fewer points per dollar the more you have, to your average [status](status) over every round, so a weak round weighs. Ending out of the rat race multiplies it, the more the sooner you got out.
guide.invest: Cash earns nothing; [savings](savings) pay a little and are safe. [Funds](index), [bonds](bond) and shares are open from the start; gold and crypto need more Finance, which a course (Lifestyle tab) or years of investing bring.
guide.focus: The Lifestyle tab holds your [focus](focus): study for a promotion, work overtime for pay now, or look for a better job. Use it every round.
guide.status: Your [status](status) comes from your job, your home, your city, how you live (Lifestyle tab) and what you buy (Shop); the score counts its average over the whole life. Living better raises your living costs, and many things cost upkeep every year and lose value.
guide.flow: [Flow](flow), at the top, is what you earn less what you spend in a year, before tax. The Taxes tab shows this round to the dollar.
guide.debt: Debt and Taxes are open now. A loan says what it costs each round before you take it; Taxes shows this round to the dollar, and what you could hide from the taxman, at a risk.
guide.rivals: "Your people" in the paper are three people your age living beside you: a classmate, a cousin and an ex. Your profile shows where you stand among them, and the end of your life ranks you.
guide.inflation: With [inflation](inflation), prices and pay tend to rise every year, but your cash does not: each round it buys less. Your score counts net worth in the money of when you were {from}, so what does not grow shrinks.
guide.property: Homes are open now: buying one costs a [deposit](downPayment) and a tax, and saves the rent. A home with a spare room can take a lodger.
guide.business: Businesses are open now: starting one takes a point of focus and money, and you run it or pay a manager. If it pays at least {share}% of your salary two rounds running, you can quit for it.
guide.move: Moving to another city is in Lifestyle, under Your city. Each city pays and costs differently, and going back home has its perks.
guide.workMode: In Lifestyle, How you work: half the day frees focus for less pay; working from home comes a few rungs up, in the trades that allow it.
guide.taxes: In Taxes you can hide part of your pay, open a company abroad, or keep crypto gains quiet. It saves money now and builds suspicion; an inspection takes it back with a fine.
guide.firstCrisis: Your first crisis: prices fall and some lose their jobs. Whoever has cash and does not sell in a panic usually comes out ahead, because what is cheap today tends to recover.
guide.firstCard: You owe money on the [credit card](creditCard), at {rate} a year: the dearest debt in the game. Pay it off before investing, because no investment earns that much.
guide.firstMargin: You bought on [margin](margin): you win and lose faster. If the asset falls far enough, the broker sells it all without asking; keep an eye on the gauge in Debt.
guide.firstMortgage: You have a [mortgage](mortgage) now. Fixed: you pay the same whatever happens. Variable: it follows rates, cheaper when they fall and painful when they rise. You can switch it in Debt.
guide.firstHalfway: Your [passive income](passive) already covers half your outgoings. Once it covers all of them two rounds running, you are out of the rat race.
guide.firstOvertime: You worked overtime last round. Two rounds running cost health, and from the third there is a {chance}% chance of burning out: more health and a point of focus less the round after. Resting that round breaks the streak.
guide.firstHiding: You are hiding money from the taxman: each round suspicion grows, and with it the chance of an inspection. One takes what you hid, a {fine}% fine on top and status; if it is a lot, there is a trial, and prison means no pay and a rung lower.
guide.firstShort: These orders leave you short: what your savings do not cover goes on the [credit card](creditCard), at {rate}. If that debt grows past three years of your income while you owe more than you own, you go bankrupt: everything is sold at a discount, status is lost for good, and no loans for years.

cash.name: Cash
cash.text: The money you have to hand. Your spending and buying come out of it; while it waits it earns nothing, and with inflation it buys less every year.

netWorth.name: Net worth
netWorth.text: Everything you own less everything you owe: cash, savings, pension, investments, homes, businesses, and what your things would sell for.

flow.name: Flow
flow.text: What comes in over a year less what goes out, before tax. Green, you have money to spare; red, you are eating into your cash.

passive.name: Passive income
passive.text: What you earn without working: dividends and coupons, savings interest, rent and businesses. Once, after tax, it pays all your outgoings two rounds running, you are out of the rat race.

status.name: Status
status.text: Points for who you are and what you have: your job, your home, your city, how you live, your things, your contacts and what cards bring. The score counts its average over the whole life, not where it ends.

focus.name: Focus
focus.text: Your spare time each round, in points. You spend it on study, overtime, a job hunt, learning, starting a business or moving, among other things.

savings.name: Savings
savings.text: A safe account that pays a little interest, up and down with rates. If you are short of cash at the end of a round, it comes from here first.

index.name: Index fund
index.text: A fund that buys a little of every company in a market. It rises and falls with the whole market, without hanging on any one company.

bond.name: Bond
bond.text: A loan to a government. It pays you interest every year, the coupon, which follows rates, and its price moves less than shares do.

creditCard.name: Credit card
creditCard.text: It covers what is missing once cash and savings run out, at {rate} a year: the dearest debt. Cash to spare at the end of a round pays it down by itself.

margin.name: Margin
margin.text: Buying with money the broker lends you, against what you buy. You win and lose faster, and if the price falls too far, the broker sells it all without asking.

mortgage.name: Mortgage
mortgage.text: A loan to buy a home, paid back over many years. Fixed: you pay the same whatever happens. Variable: the payment follows rates, up or down.

downPayment.name: Deposit
downPayment.text: The part of a home's price you pay yourself when you buy it; the rest can be a mortgage.

inflation.name: Inflation
inflation.text: How much prices rise each year, nearly always. Your pay and your costs rise with them, but cash does not. Your score counts net worth in the money of when you were {from}.

howTo.openHint: The goal, the rounds, the score, every tip and the words of the game.
howTo.goal: You live a life of {rounds} rounds of two years, from {from} to {to}, and aim to end it with the best score. Getting out of the rat race multiplies it: [passive income](passive) that pays all your outgoings.
howTo.round: You read the paper, with hints of what is coming. You answer the cards life deals you. You decide what to do with your money, and nothing happens until you play the round. Then two years go by: you are paid, you pay, prices move and you see where it all went.
howTo.score: Your [net worth](netWorth), in the money of when you were {from}, makes points on a curve that flattens: going from $10,000 to $100,000 adds 100, and from 1 to 10 million, another 100. Your average [status](status) over every round is added, not where it ends: 40 for ten rounds and 10 for ten more make 25. If you end out of the rat race, the total is multiplied, the more the sooner you got out.

crisis.advice: A crisis punishes whoever has to sell and whoever owes a lot. Those who hold usually get some of it back on the way out.

escape.title: Out of the rat race!
escape.body: At {age}, your income pays for your whole life without you. From today, work is a choice.
escape.hint: The earlier you get out, the bigger the bonus on your score. If your income stops covering your life, the wheel turns again.
escape.go: Carry on, for the fun of it

million.title: Your first million
million.body: At {age} you are worth a million real dollars: the kind that bought the same when you started.
million.hint: The second usually comes sooner than the first.

bankrupt.title: Bankrupt
bankrupt.body: At {age} your debts have beaten you. Everything you owned is sold and everything you owed is cancelled.
bankrupt.hint: No bank will lend to you until you are {age}. Your pension plan is untouched. Life goes on.

evasion.officeStrict: The tax office here is strict: inspections come more often.

family.title: At the Christmas dinner
family.room: "Still in the room? Your cousin has a flat already. Two, actually."
family.frugal: Your mother slips a lunchbox into your bag. And another one.
family.car: Your brother-in-law asks what the car cost. Then asks again, in case it changed.
family.lavish: An aunt asks, very quietly, whether you won the lottery.
family.kids: The children open their presents in four minutes. The bill took you two years.
family.plain: Someone brings up politics. You leave before dessert.

profile.title: Your life
profile.leaveHint: Your life is saved after every step.
profile.itemWhen: It is sold or cancelled during the finances: here or in the Shop tab.
profile.itemUndo: It takes effect when the round is played. Until then you can take it out of the basket.
profile.aboutLifestyle: Your lifestyle multiplies what living costs you each year. Living on little shows and takes status away; the top two give it.
profile.aboutRent: Until you own a home in {city}, you rent. A room or a flat changes what you spend and your status.
profile.rentCost: The cost is that of your whole life with that rent, at the lifestyle you lead.
profile.aboutInsurance: You pay a premium every year. In return, when a bad card comes, the insurance pays part of the bill.
profile.changedIn: It is changed during the finances: here or in the Lifestyle tab.
profile.pickHere: Tap to choose. It takes effect when the round is played.

cash.title: Cash
cash.about: The money you have on hand. Your expenses, your purchases and your taxes come out of it.
cash.note: It earns nothing, and inflation eats it. Keep what the round needs and put the rest to work.

savings.title: Savings
savings.about: A deposit with no risk. It pays interest that follows the central bank's rate.
savings.note: If you ever run short of cash, the game takes it from here first, before it goes on the credit card.

pension.title: Pension plan
pension.about: Money put aside for the end. What you pay in lowers that round's tax.
pension.note: It cannot be touched before then, whatever happens. A bankruptcy does not take it either, and it counts in your net worth.

investments.title: Investments
investments.about: What you hold in the markets, at today's price.
investments.none: You have no investments yet. They are bought in the Market tab.
investments.note: The gain is over what you paid. When you sell, the taxman takes his share of it.

homes.title: Property
homes.about: Your properties, at what they are worth today. The mortgage on each is counted apart, under Debts.
homes.note: They are sold and let in the Property tab.

things.title: Things
things.about: What you own, at what you would get for it today. Tap one to look at it.
things.note: Nearly everything loses value each year. A few watches, bags and works of art hold it or gain.

debts.title: Debts
debts.about: Everything you owe. Each round you pay interest and repay a part.
debts.note: The credit card is the dearest and has no term: it fills by itself when cash runs short. Clear it first.

netWorth.title: Net worth
netWorth.about: Everything you own less everything you owe. It is half your score; the other half is status.

businesses.title: Businesses
businesses.about: What is in each of your businesses: what it is worth today.
businesses.note: They are run, grown and sold in the Business tab.

legal.title: Privacy and legal notice
legal.noticeBody: The Rat Race is a free game of fiction. The companies, people and news in it are parodies, and nothing it says is financial advice.
legal.dataBody: Opening the game creates an anonymous guest account. If you keep it with Google, also your Google email and name. What you play: lives, records, nickname, rat, friend code, friends and games. If you turn notices on, the notification address of your browser or phone and your language. And technical errors, cleaned of anything personal, and a count of what is played (lives begun and ended, games with others) with nothing that says who you are. Your nickname and rat are seen in rankings and games.
legal.whyBody: Only to make the game work: your life on every device, the rankings, games with friends and the notices you turn on. The basis is giving you the service you ask for and, for notices, your consent, which you withdraw any time in Settings. There are no ads and we sell no data.
legal.whoBody: Supabase (accounts and database, in Japan), Vercel (the site and a count of visits with no cookies), Google, if you sign in with Google, and, in the phone app, Expo and Google's Firebase Cloud Messaging, which carry the notices to your phone if you turn them on. Outside the EU, under the European Commission's standard contractual clauses.
legal.deviceBody: We use no tracking cookies. The game keeps your life and settings in the browser, or in the app's storage on a phone, because without that it cannot be played.
legal.rightsBody: We keep it while you use the account. You can ask to see, correct, take or delete it by writing to the contact above, and complain to your data protection authority. If you are under 14, ask a parent before signing in with Google.
legal.deletionBody: In Settings, choose Delete account, on this site or in the app. If you signed in with Google, you can do it from any browser by signing in on the site. Or write to the contact above. Your account goes with everything in it: lives, records, nickname, rat, friends, games and notices. Another phone or browser where you played keeps its own copy until you delete the account there too. Anonymous counts of what is played and technical errors are kept, because they say nothing of who you are.
